nodes.name: Cron - Every 30 Min
nodes.notes: Layer 0: Heartbeat. Fires the whole pipeline every 30 minutes. RSS is cheap to poll, so 15-30 min gives near-real-time alerts without hammering any server.

nodes.name: RSS - TechCrunch (Venture)
nodes.notes: Layer 1 (best): Official RSS. Free, no auth, no scraping risk, structured <item> XML. TechCrunch publishes a dedicated Venture category feed which is heavily funding-focused, so noise is already low before AI filtering.

nodes.name: RSS - VentureBeat
nodes.notes: Layer 1: Official RSS feed. Free and reliable. VentureBeat covers enterprise/AI funding rounds that TechCrunch sometimes misses.

nodes.name: RSS - YourStory (India)
nodes.notes: Layer 1: Official RSS. Adds India-focused deal flow, which most US-centric aggregators under-report.

nodes.name: RSS - EU-Startups
nodes.notes: Layer 1: Official RSS. Adds European deal flow. Combined with TechCrunch/VentureBeat/YourStory this gives US + EU + India coverage from Layer 1 alone.

nodes.name: RSS - Google News (Funding Query)
nodes.notes: Layer 2 (fallback used proactively as a safety net): Google News RSS is free and requires no API key. Used here as a catch-all for sites that DON'T publish RSS (e.g. many regional/vertical blogs) by searching a funding-keyword query across the whole web. Query: intitle:raises OR intitle:'Series A' OR intitle:'Series B' OR intitle:seed funding, restricted to the last day.

nodes.name: RSS - VC Blog (a16z)
nodes.notes: Layer 3: VC firm blogs. VCs often announce a portfolio investment the same day the round closes, sometimes before press coverage, because they write their own post instead of waiting on a journalist. Add one HTTP/RSS node per VC you want to track (Sequoia, Accel, Y Combinator, Lightspeed, etc.) by duplicating this node.

nodes.name: IMAP - Google Alerts Inbox (optional)
nodes.notes: Layer 3b (optional): Google Alerts has no RSS anymore, only email. Point a Google Alert ('startup funding', 'series a funding', etc.) at a dedicated inbox and read it with IMAP. Disabled by default - configure IMAP credentials and set the node active if you want this source.

nodes.name: Merge All Sources
nodes.notes: Combines every Layer 1/2/3 source into a single item list (mode: Append). This is where the multi-source fan-in happens before any processing. Add more input branches here as you add more RSS/VC/blog nodes - no downstream node needs to change.

nodes.name: Normalize Fields
nodes.notes: RSS nodes from different sites return slightly different field names (title/contentSnippet/link vs title/content/link). This node maps everything into one consistent schema (title, link, content, source, pubDate) so every downstream node can rely on fixed field names regardless of which feed the item came from.

nodes.name: Deduplicate (URL + Title Similarity)
nodes.notes: Removes duplicates using three passes: (1) exact URL match, (2) normalized-title exact match (strips punctuation/case), (3) fuzzy title similarity via a simple token-overlap score, catching the common case where two outlets cover the same round with slightly different headlines.

nodes.name: AI - Detect & Extract Funding Data
nodes.notes: Single LLM call does two jobs at once to save API cost: (1) classify whether this article is actually a funding announcement, (2) if yes, extract structured JSON. Uses a cheap model (gpt-4o-mini) since this is a classification+extraction task, not open-ended reasoning. Swap for Google Gemini Flash (also has a generous free tier) if you prefer $0 cost - just replace this node with an HTTP Request to the Gemini API using the same prompt.

nodes.name: Parse AI JSON
nodes.notes: The OpenAI node returns the model's reply as a text string (even in JSON mode, n8n wraps it under message.content). This node parses that string into real fields and merges it back with the original article metadata (link, pubDate, source) so nothing is lost.

nodes.name: IF - Is Confirmed Funding Event?
nodes.notes: Gate that separates real funding events from noise. Requires is_funding = true AND confidence >= 0.7 so borderline/ambiguous AI classifications don't reach your notification channel.

nodes.name: Discard - Not a Funding Event
nodes.notes: Dead-end for the FALSE branch. Nothing happens here on purpose - this is the 'stop instead of generating poor-quality results' behavior requested for low-confidence items.

nodes.name: Filter - Business Criteria
nodes.notes: Your business rules live ONLY here. To change what you get notified about, edit these conditions in the n8n UI - nothing else in the workflow needs to change. Current defaults: amount >= $1M (or unknown/undisclosed allowed through), and not an obvious noise keyword in the title. Add/remove conditions for stage, country, or industry using the '+' button in this node.

nodes.name: Check Against Sent History
nodes.notes: Prevents re-notifying about a company already alerted (e.g. the same round covered by TechCrunch and VentureBeat a day apart). Reads previously logged source_url values from the Google Sheets 'Sent Log' tab (fetched in the node above via the Sheets node's own read) - here we simply attach a static-data cache within the same execution plus rely on the Google Sheets 'Append or Update' node downstream (matching on source_url) as the durable de-dupe layer. Replace with a lookup against Airtable/Postgres if you use those instead of Sheets.

nodes.name: Google Sheets - Log Event
nodes.notes: Free persistent storage of every confirmed, filtered funding event. Also doubles as your historical record for the duplicate-prevention logic and lets you build charts/pivot tables later without extra tooling. Swap for Airtable/Notion/Postgres/Supabase nodes if preferred - same fields.

assignments.name: message_text

nodes.name: Format Notification Message
nodes.notes: Builds one clean, reusable text block so every notification channel (Telegram/Slack/Discord/Email) sends identical, well-formatted content without duplicating formatting logic in each channel node.

nodes.name: Telegram - Send Alert
nodes.notes: Primary notification channel - free, instant, works great on mobile. Requires a Telegram bot token (via @BotFather) and your chat ID configured in credentials.

nodes.name: Slack - Send Alert (optional)
nodes.notes: Optional second channel for team environments. Disabled by default - enable and configure a Slack credential + channel if desired.

nodes.name: Merge Funding Sources
nodes.notes: Fan-in for all funding RSS sources.

nodes.name: Normalize Funding Fields
nodes.notes: Maps every feed's fields into one consistent schema.

nodes.name: Deduplicate Funding Items
nodes.notes: URL exact match + fuzzy title similarity (token overlap >= 0.75).

nodes.name: AI - Detect & Extract Funding
nodes.notes: Classifies + extracts structured funding JSON in one call (gpt-4o-mini, temperature 0).

nodes.name: Parse Funding AI JSON
nodes.notes: Parses model output, merges with article metadata.

nodes.name: IF - Confirmed Funding Event?
nodes.notes: Gate: is_funding true and confidence >= 0.7.

nodes.name: Discard - Not Funding
nodes.notes: Dead end for false branch.

nodes.name: Filter - Min Amount / Relevance
nodes.notes: Edit this node to tune what counts as a lead-worthy round. Default: amount >= $500k or undisclosed allowed through (Sreeva targets early/growth stage, so threshold is lower than a generic news filter).

nodes.name: Generate Company Key (Funding)
nodes.notes: Normalizes company name into a stable join key (company_key) used across the whole sheet so 'Acme Inc.' and 'ACME' resolve to the same row.

nodes.name: Sheets - Upsert Funding Signal
nodes.notes: Writes/updates the funding half of the company's row in 'Company Signals'. Matches on company_key so a hiring signal for the same company (from the other branch) lands on the same row.

nodes.name: Execute Sub-Workflow - Evaluate & Notify (Funding)
nodes.notes: Hands off to the shared tiering/alerting sub-workflow. REPLACE workflowId after importing 'Sreeva - Evaluate Tier & Notify'.

nodes.name: Generate ATS Slug Candidates
nodes.notes: Branch C: for a funded company, guess its Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby board slug (common pattern = lowercase company name, no spaces) so we can check EXACTLY how many roles are open on its own careers page - the most reliable hiring confirmation.

nodes.name: HTTP - Greenhouse Jobs
nodes.notes: Free public API, no key needed. Fails silently (continueOnFail) if the company doesn't use Greenhouse or the slug guess is wrong.

nodes.name: HTTP - Lever Jobs
nodes.notes: Free public API, no key needed.

nodes.name: HTTP - Ashby Jobs
nodes.notes: Free public API, no key needed.

nodes.name: Merge ATS Results
nodes.notes: Combines whichever of the 3 ATS calls actually returned data.

nodes.name: Count Open Roles (ATS)
nodes.notes: Counts jobs array length from whichever ATS responded. Attaches company_key so it can be joined back to the sheet.

nodes.name: Filter - 2+ Open Roles (ATS)
nodes.notes: Only count it as a hiring signal if the careers page confirms 2 or more open roles.

nodes.name: Sheets - Upsert Hiring Signal (ATS)
nodes.notes: Confirms the hiring half of the row for a funded company using their own careers page - the strongest possible hiring signal.

nodes.name: Execute Sub-Workflow - Evaluate & Notify (ATS)
nodes.notes: Re-checks tier now that hiring is confirmed via careers page - this is usually what flips a company from WARM to HOT.

nodes.name: HTTP - Find Latest HN Hiring Thread
nodes.notes: Free, no key. HN Algolia search API finds the current month's 'Ask HN: Who is Hiring?' story by whoishiring account.

nodes.name: Get Latest Thread ID
nodes.notes: Takes the newest matching story from the search results.

nodes.name: HTTP - Fetch HN Thread Comments
nodes.notes: Free. Returns the full thread including all top-level comments (each = one company's hiring post).

parameters.jsCode:
const children = $input.first().json.children || [];
return children.filter(c => c.text).map(c => ({ json: { comment_text: c.text, comment_url: `https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=${c.id}` } }));

nodes.name: Flatten HN Comments
nodes.notes: Extracts each top-level comment as its own item so it can go through AI extraction individually.

nodes.name: AI - Extract Company & Role Count (HN)
nodes.notes: HN hiring posts are free text, not structured - AI pulls out company name, whether they mention recent funding, and how many distinct roles are listed.

nodes.name: Parse HN AI JSON
nodes.notes: Parses the extraction and attaches the source comment URL.

nodes.name: HTTP - RemoteOK Jobs
nodes.notes: Free JSON feed of all current remote postings, no key needed.

nodes.name: Group RemoteOK by Company
nodes.notes: Counts how many distinct postings each company has in the feed - 2+ postings from the same company = active hiring push.

nodes.name: RSS - WeWorkRemotely (Programming)
nodes.notes: Free RSS. Titles follow 'Company: Job Title' format.

nodes.name: RSS - WeWorkRemotely (DevOps/Sysadmin)
nodes.notes: Free RSS, engineering-adjacent category (relevant buying signal per original brief).

nodes.name: Merge WWR Categories
nodes.notes: Combines both WWR category feeds.

nodes.name: Group WWR by Company
nodes.notes: Parses 'Company: Job Title' from RSS titles and groups by company, same 2+ threshold as RemoteOK.

nodes.name: Merge Broad Hiring Sources
nodes.notes: Combines HN + RemoteOK + WWR into one hiring-signal list.

nodes.name: Generate Company Key (Hiring)
nodes.notes: Same slugify logic as the funding branch so both branches land on the same sheet row for a given company.

nodes.name: Filter - 2+ Roles (Broad)
nodes.notes: Final gate before writing to the sheet - only companies with 2+ distinct open roles count as a hiring signal.

nodes.name: Sheets - Upsert Hiring Signal (Broad)
nodes.notes: Writes the hiring half of the row, independent of whether funding was ever detected for this company.

nodes.name: Execute Sub-Workflow - Evaluate & Notify (Hiring)
nodes.notes: Hands off to the same shared tiering/alerting sub-workflow used by the funding branch.

nodes.name: When Called by Main Workflow
nodes.notes: Receives one input: company_key. Both the funding branch and hiring branch of the main workflow call this after writing their half of the signal to the sheet.

nodes.name: Sheets - Get Company Row
nodes.notes: Reads back the FULL row for this company - including whatever the other branch may have already written - so tiering always reflects the latest combined state, not just the branch that just ran.

nodes.name: Compute Tier
nodes.notes: HOT = funded AND hiring 2+. WARM = either signal alone. Also decides whether this is worth re-notifying (tier changed since last alert), so the same company doesn't ping you every 30 minutes.

nodes.name: IF - Should Notify?
nodes.notes: Only proceeds if the tier is new or upgraded (e.g. first time WARM, or WARM -> HOT). A repeat HOT with no change is silently dropped here.

nodes.name: Sheets - Update Last Notified Tier
nodes.notes: Records that we've now alerted at this tier, so the next run doesn't repeat the same alert.
